clue.text: Ascot can provide this Marx Brothers' flick

explanation.surface: A racecourse outing is likened to a classic comedy film.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, so an outing there is a racing outing; it is also the title of a 1937 Marx Brothers comedy film.

clue.text: Worker goes to large bedroom and is asleep

indicators.note: the worker goes to, that is joins on after, the bedroom word in the answer

parts.note: a dorm (dormitory) is a large shared bedroom
an ant is the classic worker insect in crosswords

explanation.surface: A labourer heads off to a shared bedroom and falls asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive and in a sleep-like state, as a hibernating creature or a volcano at rest.

clue.text: Sailor having many chats at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mariner who talks a great deal while out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sails a private pleasure vessel is a sailor.

clue.text: Bird nibbled choice morsel

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit is the past tense of bite, so nibbled

explanation.surface: A bird pecks at a tasty scrap of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasty small piece of food, or by extension a juicy piece of gossip.

clue.text: Something popular belonging to girl is closed until now

parts.note: a hit is a popular success
her is the possessive meaning of the girl
a door that is to is pulled shut

explanation.surface: A girl's popular possession has been shut away up to the present.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning up to this point in time.

clue.text: Some golf and some drinks

explanation.surface: A golfer's day ends with drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete circuit of eighteen holes in golf; also one set of drinks bought for everyone in a group.

clue.text: What Indian waiter might bring guy at lunchtime?

parts.note: a chap is a guy, a man
lunchtime is one o'clock, and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A diner wonders what a waiter in an Indian restaurant will bring a man at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is taken as one o'clock, giving the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: An unleavened flatbread served with curries, the sort of thing brought to the table in an Indian restaurant.

clue.text: At school Venetian sages rewrite a work by Keats

indicators.note: to rewrite something is to recast it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: In class, wise men from Venice redraft a Keats poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At school' reads as a setting for the sages, but school simply supplies its abbreviation S; 'At' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative poem of 1820 by John Keats, set on the eve of a saint's feast day.

clue.text: Of course it's hot in Mexico !

definitions.text: Of course it's hot in Mexico !

parts.words: Of course it's hot in Mexico
parts.note: seemingly a remark about the weather, but read as a course of a meal: a spicy dish associated with Mexico

explanation.surface: A traveller states the obvious about Mexican weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally' but means 'as a course of a meal', and 'hot' means spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy stew of minced beef, beans and chilli peppers, Tex-Mex in origin.

clue.text: Chariot crushed bean

indicators.note: something crushed is pressed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bean is flattened beneath a charioteer's wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A small white variety of the kidney bean, used in baked beans.

clue.text: I'm with aunts, swimming in the big wave

indicators.note: letters that are swimming move about freely, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone swims with relatives and gets caught in a huge wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea wave set off by an earthquake or undersea landslide.

clue.text: Completely unlike Solomon, if nothing else

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are no Solomon, at the very least.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon was proverbially the wisest of men, so the least sage of all is utterly unlike him; the word also means at any rate.

clue.text: Preliminary sketch of Drake's first boat

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Drake's is taken

parts.note: a raft is a simple flat boat

explanation.surface: An early drawing of Sir Francis Drake's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough first version of a plan or document.

clue.text: What an orchestra should be, eventually

explanation.surface: A conductor hopes the players will keep together sooner or later.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra should keep the beat together, playing to the rhythm; the phrase also means sooner or later.

clue.text: Turns over fish that's really hot

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for turns is read backwards

parts.note: fits are turns, sudden attacks of illness
a ling is a long food fish

explanation.surface: A fish flips over because the water is too warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' here are bouts of illness, not rotations, and 'over' is the signal to read that word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppressively warm, as air that makes breathing difficult.

clue.text: While swimming I'll float with small boats

indicators.note: letters that are swimming move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer drifts along among small boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges I'LL FLOAT to FLOTILLA, and S for small is added; 'While' and 'with' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fleets of ships or vessels, so groups of boats.

clue.text: Two sailors carry a small volume up to card game

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction is read from the bottom
the sailors carry, that is hold between them, the following pieces

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
CC is a cubic centimetre, a small volume

explanation.surface: A pair of sailors haul a little book up to join a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: TAR and AB hold A and CC to make TARACCAB, which 'up' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino card game in which players bet on the hand closest to nine.

clue.text: Asiatic, say, that's after gold has books on metal, symbolically

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that's comes after the heraldic word for gold

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
i.e. (id est) means that is
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A convoluted description of someone from the East with gold, books and metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the East, especially Asia; 'say' marks Asiatic as one example of the sense.

clue.text: As an alternative this month, journalist had article inside

parts.note: inst (instant) means of this month in old business letters

indicators.note: the article goes inside the journalist's abbreviation

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: This month a reporter took on a different story.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, short for 'instant', means 'of this month' in old-fashioned letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning in place of something else, by way of substitute.

clue.text: Miner's small dog

indicators.note: small means made shorter, so the word for miner loses its last letter

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A coal worker owns a little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' cuts the R from COLLIER; the 's is not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepdog breed from Scotland, as in Border or rough breeds.

clue.text: Port the French own? That's about right !

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for own goes around the letter for right

parts.note: to have is to own

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a harbour belongs to France and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A major seaport in Normandy, at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: Group of musicians being one over the eight? Quite the opposite !

definitions.text: Group of musicians being one over the eight? Quite the opposite !

parts.words: Group of musicians being one over the eight? Quite the opposite
parts.note: one over the eight is British slang for drunk, but read literally its opposite is one under eight: a band of seven players

explanation.surface: A band is accused of being tipsy, then said to be the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for having had too much to drink; taken literally and reversed it means seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven performers, one fewer than an octet.

clue.text: Conservative enquires after vessels

indicators.note: the word for enquires comes after the abbreviation for Conservative

parts.note: asks means enquires

explanation.surface: A Tory politician asks questions about ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrels for holding liquids are containers, and vessel can mean any container.

clue.text: On the Sabbath, try to shave

parts.note: the Christian Sabbath is Sunday, abbreviated S
a judge will hear, or try, a case

explanation.surface: A man resolves to get a shave on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is the courtroom sense, as a judge tries or hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off hair or wool closely, as with a sheep's fleece.

clue.text: Loves Cheshire around start of spring

indicators.note: around means scattered about, so the county's letters are rearranged
the first letter of spring is taken

explanation.surface: Someone adores the north-west English county as spring begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England; 'around' here signals a rearrangement, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold dear and protect someone is to adore them.

clue.text: Animal eggs are expensive, we hear

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: we hear means the word for expensive is spoken and its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: Fish eggs are pricey, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Eurasian species of deer, a woodland creature.

clue.text: Oral examination to permit return to city

indicators.note: to return is to turn back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination at university
let means permit

explanation.surface: A student must pass a viva before being allowed home to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is a spoken university exam; the single indicator 'return' turns both pieces round together.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest urban centre of Israel's coastal plain.

clue.text: Tenderest meals cooked by wise old folk

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The softest dishes are prepared for sage elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior politicians respected for long experience and wisdom.
